content: As with paragraph-level valence, the writer's perspective towards the label homosexual is significantly more negative than towards gay ($ p < 0.001$). Linear regression indicates that perspectives towards noun phrases named by any LGBTQ term, gay, and American have all significantly increased over time ($p < 0.01$). However, the trends are still quite different, as the slopes for gay and all LGBTQ terms are an order of magnitude greater than American ($m =(1.1\pm 0.39)\times 10^{-4}$ for American, $m=(1.4\pm 0.18)\times 10^{-3}$ for all LGBTQ terms, and $m=(1.1\pm 0.22)\times 10^{-3}$ for gay). Furthermore, the writer's perspective towards noun phrases containing homosexual have significantly decreased over time ($p < 0.0001$).
